info.title: OpenHelm Public API
info.description: Drive OpenHelm Cloud from your own product, server-to-server. Author jobs (reusable task templates whose prompts carry {{placeholders}}), then run them with parameters and read back a structured, schema-shaped result asynchronously — with evidence (screenshot + matched text), a confidence level, and usage/cost. Task-execution failures return 200 with a structured failure_reason; HTTP 4xx/5xx is reserved for request, auth, and quota errors.

get.description: Sending identities for this org. Ensures the org default exists.

post.description: On the shared relay, or on a domain this org has verified. The webhook secret is returned ONCE.

patch.description: `autonomy` governs OUTBOUND: auto sends, notify sends and files a notice, approve_first holds for a human. `inbound_jobs_on` governs INBOUND and is the one people trip over: it defaults to `fresh` (uncorrelated mail only), so REPLIES to mail you sent do not wake a job. Any support or reply-driven workflow wants `all`.

delete.description: Refused for the org default and a project's primary identity — pause those instead.

post.description: 202 with `status`. `sent` went to SES; `pending_approval` means the inbox holds agent mail for a human and NOTHING has been delivered yet; `scheduled` will send later. `reply_to` states which address replies go to and WHY — `relay_fallback` means the branded domain cannot yet receive, so correlation runs over the relay instead. `suppressed` lists recipients dropped because they bounced, complained or opted out.

reply_to.description: Overrides the correlation Reply-To. Doing so means replies no longer thread back automatically.

send_class.description: Which daily allowance this charges. Separate counters per class, so an outreach campaign can never starve a password reset. `marketing` and conversation-opening `agent` mail carry a one-click List-Unsubscribe header and are refused if the deployment has no unsubscribe secret. Absent ⇒ derived from the caller.

scheduled_at.description: RFC 3339. Held until then by the scheduler drainer.

client_id.description: Idempotency key — a repeat returns the original send.

force_approval.description: Hold this message for human approval even when the inbox is auto.

post.description: PARTIAL SUCCESS is normal and is not an HTTP error: every item reports its own `status` and `error`, and the request is 202 regardless. A daily-cap failure stops the remainder rather than retrying it 99 times, and says so on each unattempted item.

get.description: Embeds every message in order, each with its `attachments` metadata, plus an `attachment_count` for the thread.

get.summary: Full-text search across this org's mail
List attachments on a message or a thread
get.description: Metadata only — filename, content type, size. Pass message_id or thread_id.

get.summary: Signed download URL for one attachment
get.description: Short-lived (5 min) S3 URL. Bytes never stream through the API.

get.summary: Outbound messages held for a human
get.description: The held message row IS the approval — there is no separate approvals object.

post.description: Optionally with edits. The daily cap is charged here, at release, not when it was queued.

Returns the DNS records to publish. DKIM is required to SEND; the MX record is optional and only needed to RECEIVE — which is why a verified domain can still be unable to take replies, and why reply_to may honestly fall back to the relay.

post.summary: Start or stop a sending warm-up
post.description: A brand-new domain sending at full volume gets throttled by the receiving side, and the damage outlives the campaign. Starting a warm-up caps daily volume on a rising schedule derived from the elapsed days, never stored. Transactional mail is exempt: a password reset is not volume the sender chose. An established domain being migrated should not ramp at all.
Reports SES's own answer, including FAILED — a failed DKIM check is never reported as still pending.

get.description: Each carries a `health` object DERIVED on read, never stored: `deliverable`, the `blockers` stopping it, and the last delivery/failure. A route whose domain has since lost its MX reports that, rather than remembering it once worked.

post.description: `match` is `alias@domain` or `*@domain`; `destination` must be OFF this platform — self-forwarding is a loop and is refused at write time and again at send time. Forwards re-send the original MIME byte-preserved from an SRS-signed From.

get.summary: Addresses this org must not send to

post.description: Always recorded as `manual`. A caller cannot forge a bounce, a complaint or an unsubscribe — those carry meaning only SES or a signed opt-out link is evidence for.

delete.description: Refused for an `unsubscribe`: an opt-out cannot be reversed by the sender. Re-consent happens outside this system.

post.description: `prompt` may contain {{placeholder}} tokens filled by `inputs` at run time. `input_schema.required` (if set) is validated per run. `output_schema` declares the result shape.

prompt.example: Check whether {{model_ref}} ({{finish}}) is in stock at {{supplier_url}}. Use the browser; screenshot the stock state.

patch.description: Beyond name/prompt/model, this also accepts `is_enabled`, `execution_preference` ('local_executor' to pin the job to a specific machine, via `pinned_executor_id`), and the schedule pair `schedule_type`/`schedule_config` — the pair is validated together and a type changed without its matching config is refused, never silently stored half-updated.

post.summary: Fire the job's real run right now (async)
post.description: Unlike POST /jobs/{id}/runs, this does not clone the job into a new billable API run — it starts the same run the job's own schedule or the app's "Run now" button would start, respecting `execution_preference`/`pinned_executor_id`. Returns 202 immediately with the run's id and status.

fire_at.description: Defer the run to this time instead of firing immediately.

post.description: Returns 202 immediately; poll GET /runs/{id} or supply callback_url.

output_schema.description: Overrides the job's output_schema for this run.

post.summary: Run an inline prompt (async, no pre-created job)
post.description: One-call run: pass a `prompt` (with optional {{placeholders}} filled by `inputs`) and an optional `output_schema`. Returns 202 immediately; poll GET /runs/{id} or supply callback_url. `project_id` is optional — omit it and the run executes in the org's auto-created "API Runs" project.

prompt.example: Research {{company}} and summarise its latest funding round, investors, and valuation.

project_id.description: Optional; defaults to the org's "API Runs" project.

post.summary: Jump a queued/deferred run ahead of a paused scheduler
post.description: Returns { started: false } rather than an error if the run has already started, finished, or been cancelled.

get.summary: List the plans OpenHelm Cloud offers (public, no key needed)
get.description: Prices per seat per month in minor units for USD, GBP and EUR, monthly and yearly, with the AI credits each plan pools. Cached (Cache-Control: public). A seat is an Owner, Admin or Member; Viewers are free.

get.summary: Read an account or machine setting
get.description: Account-wide keys (e.g. theme) need no executor_id. Machine-scoped keys (e.g. local_executor_backend, scheduler_paused — which coding-agent CLI a specific Mac uses, whether its local scheduler is paused) require `executor_id`; the returned value is what's REQUESTED — compare `updated_at` to `applied_at` to see whether that machine has confirmed it yet.

put.summary: Write an account or machine setting

executor_id.description: Required for a machine-scoped key; omit for an account-wide one.

get.description: Every machine (desktop app instance) that has ever attached as a cloud executor, with online status and reported capabilities.

patch.summary: Sugar over PUT /settings for a specific machine
patch.description: Set which coding-agent backend a machine uses, or whether it claims cloud-executor jobs. Takes effect the next time that machine polls, not instantly.

get.summary: List tasks OpenHelm has flagged for human attention

patch.summary: Update a task's status or resolution
patch.description: Read + status-transition only — tasks are created by OpenHelm itself, never via this API.

get.summary: Whether this account's scheduled execution is paused
get.description: Account-wide, not per-machine — see /executors/{id} for one machine's own scheduler.

post.summary: Pause ALL scheduled runs across every job and product in this account
post.description: Stops every scheduled/cron firing regardless of an individual job's own is_enabled, until /scheduler/resume is called. Does NOT affect a manual one-off run — POST /jobs/{id}/run-now and POST /runs/{id}/force are a separate path and keep working while paused.

get.summary: List agents (Goals) — standing missions, each with its own jobs

patch.summary: Update an agent's mission, name, description, or status

post.summary: Send an email from the org's identity
post.description: Sends transactionally from the org's DEFAULT address (orgname@relay.openhelm.ai). To send from a specific inbox — a product's own branded identity, or a named sender like noreply@ — use POST /inboxes/{id}/messages instead. The caller owns approval (e.g. an operator-approved body). Sets a correlation Reply-To so a reply threads back via the email.received webhook. `metadata` is an opaque object echoed verbatim on that webhook.

to.description: One address or a list. A list is ONE message whose recipients see each other.

bcc.description: Blind copies. Never written into a header the other recipients can read.

body_html.description: Pre-rendered HTML; takes precedence over body_markdown.

from_name.description: Display name before the address (defaults to the org's name).

reply_to.description: Overrides the correlation Reply-To; replies will NOT thread back.

client_id.description: Idempotency key — a repeat returns the original send instead of delivering twice.

reply_to.description: Where replies will actually land, and why. `reason` is one of sending_domain (threads on your own domain), relay_fallback (your domain has no confirmed inbound — publish its MX record), override (you supplied one; replies will not be correlated), or none (nothing verified to receive).

suppressed.description: Recipients dropped because they are suppressed (hard bounce / complaint). The message WAS delivered to everyone else. Empty on a clean send.

400.description: Email not configured / invalid body / cap reached / every recipient suppressed

get.summary: Get the org's email address + inbound callback

post.summary: Allocate the identity + set the inbound webhook callback
post.description: Allocates the org's address on first call. Set `callback_url` (https) to receive email.received webhooks. Optionally set `username` to choose a friendly address (username@relay.openhelm.ai). Returns the webhook_secret used to HMAC-sign webhooks.

username.description: Friendly email handle, e.g. "pilot-hotel-group" (3–32, a–z/0–9/-, unique).

get.description: The credentials and tools your runs can use (Gmail, GitHub, MCP servers…) with their auth status. Secrets are never returned.

post.description: Provision a connection programmatically. `type: "token"` stores an API key/secret in encrypted storage; `type: "mcp"` registers a remote HTTP/SSE MCP server by URL with optional headers (values may use ${SECRET}). For OAuth/browser providers that need a human, use POST /connections/links instead. The `secret` is write-only.

secret.description: API key/token to store (token type, or to back ${SECRET} in mcp headers).

env_var_name.description: token type: the env var the secret is injected as (e.g. GITHUB_TOKEN).

url.description: mcp type: the remote MCP server URL.

project_id.description: Scope to one project; omit for all the account's runs.

service_id.description: Which service this credential is for, as a catalogue id ("stripe", "contextely", "notion"). Service-aware features match on this and never on the connection's name, so a credential provisioned without it is stored correctly and ignored by all of them. Rejected if unknown.

400.description: Invalid type/body, or an unknown service_id

patch.summary: Update a connection (name, enabled, rotate secret)

post.summary: Mint a hosted connect link for an OAuth/browser provider
post.description: Returns a short-lived signed URL to the hosted connect flow for providers that need a browser (Google, Notion, LinkedIn…). Open it once to authorise, then poll GET /connections until the connection shows as authenticated.

name.description: Optional label for the resulting connection.

apiKey.description: Authorization: Bearer oh_live_… (mint under Settings → API & Webhooks).

TaskEnvelope.description: Shared by the poll endpoint and the completion webhook. Webhook body is { "event": "run.completed" | "run.failed", "data": <this> }.

result.description: Best-effort object conforming to the run's output_schema.

BillingHint.description: An up-front cost ESTIMATE returned with a started run. The billed figure is always usage.cost_usd on the completed TaskEnvelope; this is a planning hint only and varies with task complexity and tools used.

credit_usd_rate.description: USD value of one OpenHelm credit (1 credit = $0.05).

monthly_cap_usd.description: This API key's monthly spend cap, if set.
